summary.text: Rudy Yakym is the Republican U.S. Representative for Indiana's 2nd District. A South Bend native and business executive, he worked on the Walorski campaigns before winning the seat in a November 2022 special election after her death. He sits on the House Ways and Means Committee.

paragraphs.text: Yakym was born on February 24, 1984, in South Bend, Indiana, and his official biography describes him as a fourth-generation Hoosier raised there.
He earned an associate degree in 2009 and a bachelor's degree in 2011 from Indiana University South Bend, and later an MBA from the University of Notre Dame in 2019.
He worked as a sales manager at the broadband company Omnicity in 2010 and 2011, then served as finance director for Rep. Jackie Walorski's congressional campaign in 2011 and 2012.
From 2013 to 2019 Yakym was a vice president at the commercial real estate firm Bradley Company, and in 2015 then-Gov. Mike Pence nominated him to the Indiana Judicial Nominating Commission.
Since 2019 he has been director of growth initiatives at Kem Krest, a logistics and supply chain organization, according to his official biography and Wikipedia.

After Walorski died in an August 2022 car accident, Yakym won the Republican nomination by vote of district precinct committee members, taking it on the first ballot in a field of 12. He then won both the November 8, 2022 special election and the regular election held the same day.
He was re-elected in 2024 over Democrat Lori Camp and others and was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary.

In the 118th Congress he served on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Budget committees; since the 119th Congress he has served on Ways and Means, including its Oversight, Social Security, and Work and Welfare subcommittees.

His official biography cites the Reducing Bureaucracy to Uplift Families Act and the bipartisan Improper Payments Transparency Act as legislation he has championed, and says he helped write the tax portion of the 2025 budget reconciliation law as a Ways and Means member.
Yakym lives in Granger with his wife, Sallyann, and their three children, and serves as head usher at New Life Baptist Church, according to his official biography.
